C-TOOL-HISTORY-COMPACTION.Summary: New focused plugin `tool-history-compaction` that shrinks the replayed conversation context without touching on-disk storage, by rewriting only the in-memory message copy the model is about to receive (experimental.chat.messages.transform). It follows the DeepSeek Harness model: deterministic, model-free, non-destructive, and output-only — tool-call inputs are never modified. Compaction is tool-classified, not blanket: knowledge-bearing results (web fetch/search, skill, subagent reports) are retained because they stay relevant for the whole session, while ephemeral file/shell results (read, bash, grep, glob) are compacted aggressively because later edits of the same files supersede them. Two mechanisms: old read outputs collapse to a [Read <file>, lines X-Y] header (default on), and other ephemeral outputs are head/marker/tail pruned past a threshold. A protected recent tail, an idempotent pure-function rewrite, and a minimum-savings guard keep the provider prompt cache viable: each part is rewritten at most once, then the smaller prefix re-arms.
C-TOOL-HISTORY-COMPACTION.Problem: Every completed tool part replays its full state.input plus state.output on every subsequent turn (packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:319-320 re-emits input verbatim; output is only character-truncated). opencode.db telemetry (5041 sessions) shows the waste and its shape: median ~172k chars of tool I/O per session, ~97.5% of it older than the last message; read outputs total 328M chars (94% of all output weight, 34k reads over 2k chars), bash 76M, grep 33M, webfetch 37M. But not all of that is equally safe to drop: webfetch/web-search/skill results are session-long knowledge, while read/bash/grep outputs and edit diffs describe files that keep changing, so their older instances are quickly superseded. Prefix-cache hit rates are already 88-99% across the routing models, so most billed tokens are cheap cache-reads, but average prompt sizes (qwen3.8-max 347k, kimi-k3 327k tokens) press context limits and force LLM compactions that cost a call and lose fidelity. Replaying old read outputs also re-emits stale LINE#ID#ANCHOR anchors the model may reuse. The DeepSeek Harness compaction-tool-result-pruner already solves the output side (head + fixed marker + tail, threshold, idempotent, non-destructive, cache-aware); this change ports that model to the OpenCode plugin surface and adds the knowledge-vs-ephemeral retention split the harnesses signal (oh-my-pi protects skill/plan reads; superseded-read pruning drops reads invalidated by later edits).

Goals.Goal: New focused plugin M-PLUGIN-TOOL-HISTORY-COMPACTION (src/plugins/tool-history-compaction/), exported from the package barrel, enabled via the vvoc plugin toggle, operating only through experimental.chat.messages.transform so storage and UI diff views keep the full payload.
Output-only compaction: tool-call inputs (state.input) are never modified under any policy; only the content of state.output of completed tool parts may be rewritten.

Deterministic idempotent rewrite: compaction is a pure function of (part content, age in the message array); no wall-clock, randomness, or request-order inputs; a part already in compact form is detected by its marker and skipped, so each part is rewritten at most once and the rewritten prefix is byte-stable for prompt caching.

Tool retention classification: a configurable case-insensitive substring list `retainTools` (default covering web fetch/search, skill, and subagent families) marks knowledge results that are never compacted; all other completed tool parts are ephemeral and eligible.

readSlim (default on): replace old read outputs with [Read <file>, lines X-Y], file recovered from state.input.filePath and range from the output header when present; when the file/range cannot be determined, fall back to output pruning instead of fabricating a summary.

Output pruning (default on) for ephemeral non-read tools (bash, grep, glob, and others): replace output text exceeding outputMaxChars with headChars + fixed marker + tailChars (DeepSeek Harness shape); rich ordering preserved; Unicode-safe slicing.

Protected tail invariants: never rewrite parts in the last assistant message, the last protectLastCalls completed tool calls, parts with state.status === "error", or parts already compacted by OpenCode (state.time.compacted).
minSavingsChars guard: skip any rewrite whose compacted form is not at least minSavingsChars shorter, so sub-threshold edits do not churn the prompt cache for no gain.

Config in vvoc.json under plugins["tool-history-compaction"] (boolean-or-object), conservatively materialized into vvoc.json on sync/init like the hashline-edit routing table, strictly validated fail-loud; schema v3 widened to accept the new plugin shape without invalidating existing documents.

Constraints.Constraint: OpenCode plugin API 1.18.x: experimental.chat.messages.transform fires immediately before toModelMessagesEffect with input {} and output { messages: { info, parts }[] }; it mutates only the in-memory copy; the hook carries no model argument, so the current model is resolved from the chat.message-populated session model cache (established hashline-edit pattern).

Never change part structure: type, callID, tool, ordering, and state.status are immutable; only the content of state.output of completed tool parts may be rewritten, so Anthropic tool_use/tool_result stitching and provider replay stay intact.
Inputs are never touched: state.input is replay-stable and must remain byte-identical under every policy and tier.
Non-destructive only: never use tool.execute.after for compaction; on-disk message parts keep the full payload for the transcript and diff views.
Prompt-cache stability: rewrites must be deterministic and idempotent and must not depend on wall-clock or session-global mutable state that changes per turn.

vvoc schema v3 strictness: widening plugins additionalProperties to accept the tool-history-compaction shape must remain backward compatible; unknown keys and invalid budgets still fail loudly; no silent migration.
Plugins share the startup config snapshot; config changes require an OpenCode restart (established invariant).
Do not interfere with OpenCode's own compaction placeholder ("[Old tool result content cleared]") or its summarizer; skip such parts.
DeepSeek Harness compaction-tool-result-pruner (MIT) is a behavioral reference only, not a code dependency; nothing is copied verbatim from proprietary harness sources.
Character budgets are not token budgets (DeepSeek Harness caveat); char-based thresholds and the minSavingsChars guard are the proxy, with token-level budgets deferred.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Compaction of tool-call inputs of any kind (old_string/new_string, patchText, hashline edits, etc.).
LLM summarization or replacing OpenCode's compaction/summarizer.
Changes to hashline-edit edit/read semantics, its routing table, or its anchored read transform.
Bitmap/vision compression (oh-my-pi snapcompact) or provider-native compact endpoints (codex /compact).
Token-accurate budgets; live config reload; content-aware retention rules beyond tool-name classification.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Given a real SDK-shaped messages array with historical completed tool parts, the transform hook deterministically rewrites eligible outputs; running it twice over the same input yields byte-identical output (idempotence), and a second pass over already-compacted parts performs no further change.
Retained tools (matching retainTools) have their outputs left byte-identical regardless of size; a webfetch/web-search/skill/subagent result survives compaction untouched.

readSlim on: an old read part becomes [Read <file>, lines X-Y]; a read whose filePath is absent or whose line range cannot be recovered from the header falls back to output pruning and never fabricates a summary.

Output pruning: an over-threshold ephemeral output is replaced with exactly headChars code points, the fixed marker, then tailChars code points, never exceeding outputMaxChars and strictly smaller than the input; an under-threshold output is left untouched; slicing never splits a surrogate pair.
state.input is byte-identical before and after compaction for every part, under every policy.
The last assistant message, the last protectLastCalls completed tool calls, error parts, and time.compacted parts are never modified by any layer.
Structure invariants hold under compaction: callID/type/tool/order unchanged; a tool_use/tool_result pairing test asserts the assistant tool parts still pair with their results after rewrite.
minSavingsChars guard: a rewrite whose savings fall below the threshold is skipped (test asserts no churn on a near-threshold output).

Config: plugins["tool-history-compaction"] parses boolean-or-object strictly; defaults materialize into vvoc.json on sync without overwriting user values; invalid budgets/unknown keys fail loudly at load; an existing v3 document with the new plugin key still validates against the widened schema.

Fresh full suite passes: bun test, bun run check, bun run build; bunx @osovv/grace-cli@rc lint --path . and status --path . pass with the new active bundle; bun run pack:check when the public export surface changes.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/plugins/tool-history-compaction && bun run check && bun run build && bunx @osovv/grace-cli@rc lint --path . && bunx @osovv/grace-cli@rc status --path .
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Targeted tests built on real SDK part shapes (lesson-plugin-tests-match-real-sdk-shapes); fresh full-suite pass; grace lint/status green with the new active bundle; post-release rerun of the opencode.db telemetry extraction showing a reduced median tool-I/O replay weight per session and retained webfetch/search outputs, with no change to cache-hit-rate slope for sessions with the plugin enabled.

Assumptions.Assumption: experimental.chat.messages.transform fires on every prompt build with the full in-memory message list and only the in-memory copy is mutated (verified against OpenCode v1.18.18 session/prompt.ts:1255-1262 and message-v2.ts:290-323); assumed stable across host 1.18.x patch releases.
The transform hook does not receive the current model, but no layer needs it: output compaction and retention are model-agnostic, so no session model cache is required for this plugin.
Tool part shape in the hook matches message-v2.ts: part.type === "tool", part.tool, part.callID, part.state.{status,input,output,time,metadata}.
read input carries filePath and the read output header encodes the line range when available (confirmed from opencode.db); when absent the fallback is pruning, not guessing.

Case-insensitive substring matching against tool names is a sufficient retention classifier for the default list (web fetch/search, skill, subagent families); edge-case tool families can be pinned via the configurable retainTools list.

Deterministic idempotent rewrites keep the provider prompt cache viable: each part invalidates the prefix at most once at the point of first rewrite and the smaller prefix re-arms afterward, matching the DeepSeek Harness documented behavior (pruned prefix eligible for reuse while route, envelope, and preceding history remain identical).

Compaction is safe to enable by default because it is non-destructive, cache-aware, tail-protected, idempotent, and input-preserving; users who prefer full fidelity can disable the plugin or set outputMaxChars to 0.
